title: What the code text does not settle
question: Which of the rules the other screens asked about are not settled by the City code text?
finding: 5 of the questions raised by the permit and jobs screens are not settled here: State deadlines, fee history, small-business permit renewals, discretionary-review rules and reviewer assignment.
how: Each open item from the site’s “How the permit process works” page (toConfirm), the site’s “City jobs: titles, hiring and pay” page and the site’s “Drawings and repeat winners” page was looked for in the export by section heading and key phrases.
limits: A search that finds nothing is not proof that no rule exists; rules can sit in departmental bulletins, Commission resolutions or State law.

rows.item: State deadlines for housing permits (completeness in 15 business days; comments in 30 or 60 days)
rows.why: These are State law, not San Francisco code; the export holds only the City codes. The City’s own review deadlines (21, 30 and 14 days) are in the review-metrics tables (permit_metrics).

rows.item: Fee schedules by year (Building Inspection Table 1A-A, Planning, Fire, Public Works, Public Health)
rows.why: The export prints only the current tables; earlier years need the archived ordinances.

rows.item: Renewal periods and fees for sidewalk tables and chairs, displays, parklets, food trucks and Fire operating permits
rows.why: Not checked in this pass; the Public Works and Fire Codes are in the export and can be read for it.

rows.item: Who may ask for discretionary review, its fee, and any rule against paying to withdraw a request
rows.why: The Planning Code bars discretionary review for many project types, section by section; no general rule on paying to withdraw a request was found by text search.

rows.item: How plan reviews are assigned to reviewers (rotation, district, specialty)
rows.why: The code sets the order-of-receipt rule (3.400(b)) and requires written departmental guidelines; the guidelines themselves are not in the code.

sources.t: American Legal Publishing: San Francisco Charter and Municipal Codes, full-text export (saved 17 Nov 2026)
